02 / FOLLOW THE SIGNAL

A path you can
understand.

A typical passive-guitar journey. The tone circuit is a branch, and actual layouts and control order vary. This is an educational map, not an electrical simulation.

01Pickup02Selector03Volume04Tone branch05Output

Pickup

The starting point

A passive pickup supplies the signal. Its electrical properties interact with the controls and the load; a wire colour alone does not establish a coil function.

Understand pickup conductors ↗Inspect the circuit ↗

Selector

Choose a pickup path

The selector closes particular contact pairs. Intermediate positions on a conventional five-way can connect adjacent throws. Inspect the actual contact model and verify your hardware.

Learn about selector contacts ↗Explore closed contacts ↗

Volume

Control the output

The volume pot provides a resistive track and a wiper. Its value and position affect loading and the electrical output. A supported single-pickup comparison makes the interaction easier to explore.

Understand potentiometers ↗Compare in Signal Lab ↗

Tone branch

Shape the response

A typical tone control and capacitor form a branch toward ground. The main signal does not need to pass through the tone capacitor on its way to the output. The connection depends on wiring style.

Understand capacitors and treble bleeds ↗Explore the volume bypass ↗

Output

Signal and return

The jack tip carries the output signal and the sleeve provides the return. Shielding has its own physical role even where bonded to the same ground network.

Read about ground and output ↗Find the solder destinations ↗
